summary: Re-ran /app/backend/tests/test_iter30_partner_center_routing.py after the truthy-tuple fix at server.py:3811. All 10/10 tests now PASS, including the two previously failing tests (test_pending_txn_visible_to_PA_only and test_PB_with_fake_C1_history_still_blocked). Verified the patch correctly unpacks (allowed, _reason) from _can_partner_approve before gating partner_cross visibility.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix at server.py:3811 is correct — explicitly unpacks (allowed, _reason) tuple from _can_partner_approve. Recommend adding a type annotation/docstring on _can_partner_approve to prevent regression where future callers treat the tuple as a single bool.

Consider adding a unit-level invariant: any callsite of _can_partner_approve must unpack two values; could be enforced with a mypy check or a thin wrapper helper is_partner_allowed() returning only the bool for boolean-context use.
test_credentials: admin@finance.app / Admin@123 (used by test fixtures to seed partners/centers/transactions)
seed_data_creation: Test file auto-creates TEST_iter30_*_<run>@finance.app users (PA, PB, HR, centers C1/C2, transactions) and cleans up after the run via existing fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-30 partner-role approval isolation is fully green (10/10). server.py:3811 now correctly handles the (bool, reason) tuple from _can_partner_approve. No further action needed on this scope.
rca of the issue: Previous failure RCA: _can_partner_approve was refactored to return a (bool, reason_str) tuple, but the caller at server.py:3811 used `if await _can_partner_approve(...)` which evaluates the non-empty tuple as truthy regardless of the bool value — causing PB to see C1 transactions and bypassing the cross-approve hard gate. Mitigation (applied): explicitly unpack `allowed, _reason = await _can_partner_approve(user, t); if allowed:`. Re-test confirms isolation restored.
